subject: Exec workshop — floorflow, remote-lane topology and travel liaison
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2027-05-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Exec workshop — floorflow, remote-lane topology and travel liaison

Team —

Following up on last week's planning call: Acme wants a single-day executive workshop in San Diego (June 21). They expect ~40 onsite attendees and ~30 remote seats distributed across three breakout rooms + a master boardroom. We need to lock a venue footprint, AV scope, and the travel/arrival plan for the six VIPs (two execs flying in from EU).

Key asks from me: please review and reply with concrete inputs by EOD Tuesday (May 26). I attached the latest site sketch with proposed room assignments. Focus areas:
- Boardroom rig requirements (single 16x9 feed + 4 mic zones + interpreter output)
- Breakout rooms: simple A/V (projector + BYOD HDMI), and one room must have gallery view for remote participants
- Telepresence lane: we need deterministic bridge capacity and a local transcode option if upstream bandwidth drops
- Travel liaison: who will coordinate VIP airport pickup, hotel rooming, and on-site host desk?

Attachments: site_sketch_v2.pdf (draft)

I'll loop in venue and preferred AV vendor once we have internal confirmation.

—Olga
Olga Petrov

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop — floorflow, remote-lane topology and travel liaison

Olga —

Looks good. Quick notes after reading the sketch:
- Grand Harbor (venue candidate) can fit boardroom + 3 breakouts on the mezzanine; power outlets are limited in breakout B (only two floor boxes). We'll need a small distro or run a silent generator feed if exhibitor stalls show up.
- For interpreter output: recommend discrete analog outputs (RCA) in addition to Dante stream — some of Acme's exec aids only accept line-level analog.
- Travel liaison: I can own VIP travel coordination and block the rooming list. I'll coordinate with our travel desk and provide flight arrival windows by Thursday.

Vendor note: Echo AV handled our Q4 offsite and has a lightweight fiber-as-backup option. Their basic rider is small; see vendor_rider_echo.txt (attached).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Executive Programs | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

From: Denise Harper <denise@grandharborhotels.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-26T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop — floorflow, remote-lane topology and travel liaison

Hi Olga/Laura —

Thanks for the sketch. A couple of operational constraints from our side:
1) Rigging limit on Mezzanine A is 200kg — we can hang a 2x1 LED but anything larger requires rigging review and an extra day of load-in.
2) House internet is 1Gbps burstable to 2Gbps, but sustained upstream for large cloud meetings is often variable during high activity (we see slowdowns between 07:30-10:00 PT when conferences check in).
3) We do have a dedicated green room with secure access for the VIPs; valet and a hotel shuttle to the airport can be reserved.

If you want pre-provisioned fiber for the telepresence lane, we can bring a bonded 10Gbps link for the day (cost estimate in the attachment).

—Denise

Date: 2027-05-26T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec workshop — floorflow, remote-lane topology and travel liaison

Looping in Echo AV and James from Acme for tech confirmation.

Echo — can you confirm the following items and attach your recommended "zoom lane" config? We're proposing:
- Primary bridge via our hosted vendor (Gov tier not required), with Echo providing edge transcode in the venue for gallery+interpretation mixes.
- A redundant outbound path (bonded LTE) for the bridge in case hotel uplink drops below 200Mbps.
- 4 mic zones in boardroom (table, lectern, audience-left, audience-right) with redundant feeds to the production mix.

James — Acme prefers discrete interpreter streams (EN/ES) in the master mix and wants gallery view in Breakout C with active Q&A channel.

Attachments: zoom_lane_config.pdf (Echo please confirm), vendor_rider_echo.txt

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Thanks everyone — consolidating next steps and owners: (timeline to finalize by June 4)

1) Venue confirmation and rigging: Denise to confirm mezzanine rigging allowance and cost for bonded fiber (owner: denise@grandharborhotels.com).
2) AV scope and tech doc: Echo to confirm zoom_lane_config.pdf and provide final signal path + redundancy plan (owner: ops@echotechav.com).
3) Power and distro: Marcus to source local distro and confirm onsite electrician hours (owner: marcus_lin@redwood.ai).
4) VIP travel & hotel: Laura to finalize arrivals, rooming list, and shuttle windows (owner: laura_bennett@redwood.ai).
5) Interpreter & streams: Karthik to confirm discrete interpreter output routing into the bridge and test windows (owner: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai).
6) On-site host desk & run-of-show: Olga to produce final run-of-show with load-in windows and contact sheet; will share by June 10.

Attachments included in thread: site_sketch_v2.pdf, vendor_rider_echo.txt, zoom_lane_config.pdf

If no objections, I'll lock the Grand Harbor hold today and get deposit terms from Denise.

—Olga
